content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with an analog input and a timer to measure pressure decay over time. The current pressure value is displayed on the [product_name] screen. I want to record the pressure value at both the start and end of a test, then display the difference (P1-P2). To do this, I need to store the analog input value at the test's start. I would normally use an edge detection to move the current value to a memory flag, but I'm unsure how to do this in [product_name]. Could someone advise on achieving this? I tried using an analog multiplexer but ran into a recursion error. Thank you, [user_name]
I have attached a possible solution.

Thank you—I've reviewed this and it's exactly what I needed. The math function with 'retain last value' set works similarly to a memory move operation in [version_no]. This solves the issue I was facing.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced difficulty capturing and storing analog input values at specific events using [product_name], finding the process less intuitive compared to memory move operations in [version_no] PLCs. The math function with 'retain last value' enabled offered a solution, allowing the user to overcome initial conceptual and implementation issues—including a recursion error with the analog multiplexer. Cooperative feedback led to a successful resolution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to easily store and retrieve analog values at defined events, similar to straightforward memory move operations found in [version_no] devices, without running into recursion errors or complex solutions.
